identity.summary: The Izzet League is the blue-red guild of Ravnica: a dragon-led culture of elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, and volatile discovery. The expanded story pass adds concrete examples of this identity at multiple levels: Trenz on Experiment Day, Madarrak and Castan pursuing Erno Zslod, lower-rank attendants fighting for recognition, and Ral Zarek directing crisis-scale resonator and beacon operations.
identity.philosophy: The Izzet League turns blue-red curiosity into elemental magic, mizzium technology, civic engineering, spell engines, and prototypes. Its best work makes discovery useful; its pressure point is volatile experimentation that can outrun care, procedure, or restraint.
identity.central_tension: Izzet discovery wants to move fast enough to find the breakthrough while remaining useful enough to repair, rebuild, or stabilize what the experiment affects.
identity.display_tagline: Invent first. Stabilize later.
identity.mechanics: Replicate, overload, and jump-start are the source-backed Izzet mechanics expression: scalable spell copying, spells powered from single targets into sweeping effects, and second-chance instant or sorcery casting. Mizzium devices and the resonator network are story-technology texture rather than standalone rules mechanics, and should only support Izzet when they point back to experimental invention, spellcraft, and volatile civic engineering.

LOREHOLD.name: Lorehold College

identity.summary: Lorehold is Strixhaven's College of Archaeomancy: red-white history magic expressed through artifacts, ancient tomes, spirits, scrolls, field expeditions, and the tension between orderly preservation and chaotic discovery. Its strongest verified pattern is not generic nostalgia, but active investigation of the past through records, ruins, relics, living spirits, and dangerous fieldwork.
identity.philosophy: The College of Archaeomancy believes the past is not merely interesting but essential. Understanding history is how you predict the future. Every ruin contains a lesson. The dead are not silent if you know how to ask. Lorehold scholars are simultaneously the most scholarly and most physically reckless people in any room.
identity.central_tension: Does history belong to order or to chaos? To careful systematic analysis or dangerous fieldwork? The college needs both traditions. Every student must choose - and then watch the choice shape everything afterward.
identity.display_tagline: Leave no stone unturned.
identity.mechanics: Lorehold mechanics are best read as archaeomancy in action: Spirit and statue magic, The Rousing, Spirit tokens, historical artifact restoration, and field evidence turning the past into present action. Magecraft, Learn, and Lessons are Strixhaven-wide support texture here rather than Lorehold-exclusive proof; they should only support Lorehold when paired with history, artifacts, spirits, records, ruins, or fieldwork.

gate.prompt: When the ground shifts, what do you trust first?

answers.copy: I start with agency: the private decision, the necessary edge, the first motion I can own.

answers.title: The threshold in the self
answers.copy: I listen for the moment where desire, danger, and choice become too clear to outsource.

answers.title: A braided witness
answers.copy: I want each part of the situation named, given weight, and brought into one accountable center.

answers.title: The common root
answers.copy: I trust the pattern that keeps people, place, and continuity from splintering under strain.

answers.title: The measure outside the map
answers.copy: I trust the constraint that does not ask the old language for permission before it becomes real.

gate.prompt: When pressure gathers, what should it become?

answers.title: A form that can hold
answers.copy: Pressure should become structure: named, testable, and steady enough to keep harm from spreading.

answers.title: Answerable motion
answers.copy: It should move, but with a visible thread back to responsibility, memory, and consequence.

answers.title: Many currents, one course
answers.copy: It should become a working convergence: different forces kept distinct, then aimed together.

answers.title: A wild release
answers.copy: It should become adaptation, appetite, heat, and movement before a brittle answer snaps shut.

answers.title: A silent axis
answers.copy: It should become a hard boundary: not loud, not ornamental, simply outside the usual bargain.

answers.title: The cold pattern
answers.copy: Before the room gets loud, I notice leverage, implication, and what the facts are already costing.

answers.title: The measured trace
answers.copy: I look for the thread beneath the feeling: the sign that tells me what kind of change is possible.

answers.title: The whole chord
answers.copy: The signal arrives as a chord: thought, hunger, duty, feeling, and life all audible at once.

answers.title: The live spark
answers.copy: I hear what wants to move: the heat, the honesty, the flash before it gets explained away.

answers.title: The unlit edge
answers.copy: The first signal is absence: a clean edge where the usual symbols stop being useful.

gate.prompt: What cost can an oath fairly ask of you?

answers.title: Preserve what must not break
answers.copy: It can ask me to carry the old weight: shelter, consequence, and the line that keeps faith intact.

answers.title: Steward the change
answers.copy: It can ask discipline from me: not refusal of change, but care over what change consumes.

answers.title: Keep the whole covenant
answers.copy: It can ask me to hold every claim in view, even when no single hunger deserves the throne.

answers.title: Become the changed thing
answers.copy: It can ask me to release the prior shape and become the answer the threshold requires.

answers.title: Stand where the lamp does not reach
answers.copy: It can ask a clean refusal: no borrowed brightness, no decorated answer, only the boundary kept.

answers.title: Intervene immediately

answers.title: Restore belonging

answers.title: Choose the urgent case

answers.title: Heal the bond

answers.title: Make it a debt

answers.title: Run the experiment
